newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice rate seen rising on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice rate seen rising on foreign demand.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to rise next week on foreign demand, particularly from the Philippines, exporters said on Thursday.

"The Philippines has shown interest in Pakistan's IRRI-6 variety rice and it is likely to buy a good quantity," said Javed Islam Agha, chairman of the Lahore-based Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan (REAP), but gave no further details.

The Philippines' state-owned National Food Authority is considering buying rice from two private groups in Pakistan, Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero told reporters in Manila on Thursday. He gave no details.
Agha said the outcome of negotiations between the private exporters and the Philippine importers would be known in a few days. He said substantial quantities could be involved.

An official at the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said Iraqi buyers had purchased some 42,000 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice in December from a private exporter, but the rice had not been shipped pending clearance from the United Nations' food-for-oil programme and payment from the buyers.
The RECP official said IRRI-6 prices were likely to rise if dealers got firm orders from the Philippines.
Rice exports fell 40 percent to 139,132 tonnes worth $41 million in January from 232,231 tonnes worth $56 million in December.
In the first seven months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), rice exports rose 14.7 percent to 808,453 tonnes worth $237 million from 704,880 tonnes worth $238 million in the year-ago period.
